concept-disambiguation pairwise separation: 10 confusable name-pair(s) discovered - 1 undrawn, 4 one-sided, 5 mutual

A pair is CONFUSABLE when its two names collide by spelling alone, in one of three
ways: homonym (identical once the parenthetical gloss is stripped), permuted (the
same words in a different order), or near (within 2 edits AND sharing a head or
tail run of 5+ characters, so a bare family root is not enough).
Pairs are DISCOVERED from the names themselves, never declared, so landing a
near-twin name raises the bar automatically. Being clean per-row does not separate
a pair: a concept in a large family satisfies `disambiguated` by naming ANY sibling,
while the twin it is genuinely mistakable for goes undrawn.

  x undrawn    neither names the other - the twins sit in the catalog unseparated
  > one-sided  drawn from one side only - a reader arriving at the other is unwarned
  = mutual     both name each other - a reader arriving from EITHER side is told

  x [near    ] 'SessionKey'     'SessionKeys'
      1 edit(s) apart sharing 10 characters: sessionkey / sessionkeys   (sessionkey / sessionkeys)
  > [homonym ] "Session'Q (a)" --> "Session'Q (b)"
      both are plainly named 'sessionq' once the gloss is stripped   (sessionquote1 / sessionquote2)
  > [near    ] 'CacheTTL1h' --> 'CacheTTL5m'
      2 edit(s) apart sharing 8 characters: cachettl5m / cachettl1h   (cachettl1h / cachettl5m)
  > [near    ] 'SessionKey' --> 'SessionRef'
      2 edit(s) apart sharing 7 characters: sessionref / sessionkey   (sessionkey / sessionref)
  > [permuted] 'Cache Meta (store)' <-- 'MetaCache'
      same words in a different order: cache meta   (cachemeta / metacache)
  = [homonym ] 'Decision (kernel)' <-> 'Decision (scheduler)'
      both are plainly named 'decision' once the gloss is stripped   (decisionkernel / decisionsched)
  = [homonym ] 'GatePolicy' <-> 'gate_policy'
      both are plainly named 'gatepolicy' once the gloss is stripped   (gatepolicy1 / gatepolicy2)
  = [homonym ] 'Q"uo\'te (one)' <-> 'Q"uo\'te (two)'
      both are plainly named 'quote' once the gloss is stripped   (quoteboth1 / quoteboth2)
  = [near    ] 'CycleA' <-> 'CycleB'
      1 edit(s) apart sharing 5 characters: cyclea / cycleb   (cyclea / cycleb)
  = [near    ] 'SessionRef' <-> 'SessionRow'
      2 edit(s) apart sharing 8 characters: sessionref / sessionrow   (sessionref / sessionrow)

dangling references: 1
